_what: Reproduction of the owner's loop defect: 'once I go through the other side, I stay on plane b and continue to fall through collision on plane A, which is most of the collision, and there's no easy way to get back'.

_build.note: server ROM byte-compared against disk before any measurement; a stale 741905-byte image was reloaded first

_method.instrument: record-mode write watchpoint on Sst.layer at $FF902B (player base $FF8FFE + $2D)
_method.why_watchpoint: a per-frame sampled read under-samples: an 8px cell is crossed in under one frame at gsp $600. The watchpoint records EVERY write, so the toggle count is exact rather than sampled.
_method.placement_rule: camera written and settled 12 frames BEFORE the player, or the player lands outside the streamed collision cache
_method.debug_exit: emulator/press b — NEVER by writing debug_flag ($FF903A), which skips Player_DebugExit and leaves mappings on Map_TestObj (address error in RefreshSpritePieceCount)

runs.label: leftward entry — THE OWNER'S DIRECTION

crossover_writes.note: x 1151 is the loop's bottom-CENTRE (void centre x 1148), not an arc foot

runs.verdict: ODD. Exits on plane B. y 829 is 253px BELOW ground_solid_y 576 — he fell through plane-A collision, exactly as reported.

runs.label: rightward entry

speed_collapse.note: 9px of travel in 18 frames — this is the 'can't get past it coming from the left' complaint

runs.verdict: ODD. Crosses to B and then STALLS on the arc at gsp $8E. Never reaches the top-centre mark.

runs.label: rightward from x 1070 — DISCARDED as a control
runs.why_discarded: he fell before reaching the mark, so the zero is 'never arrived', not 'arrived and did not fire'. Run B replaced it with a grounded pass. Recorded so the discard is visible rather than silent.

static_check.shipped_table: 256 slots, 2 marked, 0 holding the reserved value 3
static_check.consumption: proven by the gate: 2 marks changed Sst.layer BECAUSE a CrossoverTable byte changed and nothing else did; the unmodified table is the control
static_check.meaning: BOTH marks are present in the ROM and BOTH are consumed. The defect is NOT a missing or unbaked mark.

finding.measured: Every traversal tested toggles the layer exactly ONCE, in both directions. The player therefore always ends on plane B, which carries only ground + the RIGHT half; plane A carries most of the collision, so he falls through everything.
finding.primary_defect: The bottom-centre mark is plane-keyed, not direction-keyed (rule R2 raises on self-marks, so a plane-A player reads XOVER_TO_B regardless of travel direction). A LEFTWARD traveller therefore crosses to B at the bottom centre and immediately has no left arc to stand on, because the left half is solid only on A.
finding.secondary_defect: Rightward entry bleeds gsp $600 -> $FC over 18 frames and stalls on the arc, so it never reaches the top-centre mark either. This is the owner's original screenshot complaint.
finding.not_yet_established: Whether a traversal at a speed high enough to survive the arc reaches the top-centre mark and toggles back. No run in this set completed a circuit, so the second mark has never been observed firing.

two_defects_separated_by_trajectory._why: Hub ask 2026-09-05: his two reports may have different causes and were being treated as one. Separated here by direction of travel, with the evidence class marked per row.

westward.report: leftward entry, crosses to plane B and falls through collision
westward.path_over_built_ground: crossed at x 1151 (col 143), ended x 665 (col 83); aurora measures main ground row 72 spanning cols 58..151, so EVERY column on that path has floor
westward.cause: plane. He fell through ground that exists, for ~480px of travel. The level-edge account cannot produce this because he never reached an edge.
westward.open_question: is editor row 72 solid on BOTH planes or A-only? §3.3 requires both. His words -- 'fall through collision on plane A, which is most of the collision' -- read as a report that it is A-only. If A-only, THAT is the root cause of the westward fall, not the mark rule.
westward.status: NOT addressed by the ground extension east; that extension is about the other trajectory

eastward.evidence: INFERRED for causation, MEASURED for the geometry (aurora's extents)

my_corroborating_run.note: discarded as a crossover control for an unrelated reason, but as evidence for the edge account it fits: eastward, past x1280, nothing at any depth

eastward.geometry: aurora: main ground row 72 ends at col 151 = x1215 = the loop's right foot; first column with NO floor below y576 is col 160 = x1280; nothing from there to the section edge at x2047; cols 156-158 carry a ledge at y848
eastward.cause: the built ground ends at the loop's right foot. A rightward exit runs off the end of the level.
eastward.ruling: aurora extends the test ground east to the section edge, solid on both planes (hub, in the owner's place, 2026-09-05). Lands as its own commit BEFORE the direction-keyed verification, so the rightward circuit is measured against ground that exists.

two_defects_separated_by_trajectory._consequence: These are two defects, not one. Fixing the mark rule cannot fix the eastward fall, and extending the ground east cannot fix the westward one.

both_planes_falsification_attempt._what: Aurora's account predicts: a player handed to the WRONG plane anywhere over x464..x2047 now stays upright and is merely wrong-planed. Their framing, deliberately: 'I would rather your drive tried to BREAK the both-planes account than confirm it.'
both_planes_falsification_attempt._method: player placed on the ground (y_pos 556) at each x with Sst.layer FORCED to 1 (plane B), camera settled 14 frames first, then 50 frames run. Upright = y_pos still ~557; fallen = y_pos grows without bound.
both_planes_falsification_attempt._what_would_have_refuted_it: any test point falling. A fall anywhere in the span refutes the account regardless of how well the story reads.

points.why_this_x: middle of the old A-ONLY band (cols 88-127 = x704..x1023)
the EXACT former boundary — the column where B-solidity used to stop and where the westward fall began
inside the new east extension, where before there was no floor at any depth
near the section edge (2047) — the end of the extension, where an off-by-one in 'extend to the edge' would show

both_planes_falsification_attempt.verdict: The account SURVIVED the attempt at all four points. Layer stayed 1 throughout, so these are genuine wrong-plane stands and not a silent toggle back to A.
both_planes_falsification_attempt._scope_limit: FOUR SAMPLED POINTS, not 'everywhere over x464..x2047'. They were chosen as the ones most able to fail — the old A-only band, its exact boundary, the new ground, and the extension's far end — but a sampled pass is not a proof over the span. A column-by-column assertion would need a static check over the baked plane data, not a drive.
